speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our assessment, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if they have been progressive?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; since the clumsiness is worse on your right side, could you tell me if you have any weakness, numbness, or vision changes, and have you noticed any issues with your speech or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and one year of natalizumab use, combined with new-onset asymmetric ataxia, this strongly suggests PML, a rare opportunistic infection of the white matter. I would like to confirm this with imaging; REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI_with_contrast.
